api.endpointsIntro: Public data plane of this collection.
api.pathParamsNote: `:workspace` is the workspace UUID; `:collection` is the collection key, not its id.
api.authAnonymous: No Authorization header — anonymous principal (rights of the public role).
api.authToken: Authorization: Bearer mlp_… — the token's consumer role, intersected with its scopes.
api.grantNotice: Access is a grant. Without a read grant for the principal's role the answer is 404, indistinguishable from a collection that does not exist. That is deliberate: existence is never leaked.
api.rateLimitNote: Fixed 60-second window. These are documented contour defaults — the service does not report them over the API; the values come from the collections-service ConfigMap.
api.sampleNote: Built from this collection's actual fields. The public projection carries no service fields — no project_id, no version, no schema_version.
api.snippetsIntro: Generated from the current schema — copy and run.
api.tokensIntro: Opaque mlp_ credentials for the public plane.
api.tokensEmptyHint: Anonymous access needs no token — issue one only to give a caller more than the public role has.
api.tokensUnavailable: Token management is not reachable on this contour: the gateway does not proxy /v1/workspaces/:id/tokens or /roles. The cloud gateway routes both; on self-host, update gw-service.
api.expiryNeverWarning: A token that never expires can only be retired by hand.
api.noConsumerRoles: This workspace has no consumer role. A token can only be issued against one — admin roles are never wrapped into a credential.
api.secretOnceWarning: Shown once. The server keeps only a hash — the value cannot be seen again, only rotated.

access.statusPublicNoFields: The read grant exists but its allow-list is empty — responses carry an empty data.
access.statusPrivateHint: The public role holds no read grant — the public plane answers 404.
access.statusAuthenticated: The authenticated role reads it too: any signed-in user, workspace members included.
access.rolesIntro: Roles live on the workspace, grants on the collection. A role on its own grants nothing.
access.rolesEmpty: No roles. That usually means the workspace is half-created: five built-in roles are seeded with it.
access.kindHint: consumer — public API and tokens; admin — the panel. Kind is immutable after creation.
access.builtinImmutableHint: A built-in role cannot be renamed or deleted
access.deleteRoleConfirm: Delete the role? Its grants cascade away. A role held by a member or a token cannot be deleted.
access.membersIntro: One role per person: adding someone already listed changes their role. A person you add becomes a member of the workspace, with page editor rights in it; removing them takes both away.
access.membersNonMemberNote: A signed-in user who is not listed here does not read with nothing — they read with the built-in authenticated role. A member reads with it plus their own role, so removing them takes away only the role's rights: if authenticated holds a read grant they keep seeing the collection.
access.membersEmpty: No members. That usually means the workspace is half-created: its owner becomes a member together with it. Panel access comes from ownership, not membership; on /data a member reads with authenticated plus their own role.
access.memberFilterHint: Pick from the workspace's members — by username or email. Invite anyone who is not in the workspace by email.
access.memberFilterEmpty: The workspace has no other members yet.
access.memberNotInWorkspace: This person is not in the workspace — invite them by email.
access.memberInviteNeedsEmail: Type the full email address to send an invite.
access.memberCandidatesError: Could not load the workspace members.
access.memberUnknown: Profile not received — showing the member id
access.removeMemberConfirm: Remove the member? They lose the rights of their role, but on the /data plane they keep what the built-in authenticated role's grants give any signed-in user.
access.grantsIntro: A tick is a role's grant on an action against this collection. Revoking takes effect immediately.
access.grantsEmptyRoles: No roles — nothing to grant to.
access.failClosedNote: Public access is the public role's read grant, not a flag. Without it the public plane answers 404, indistinguishable from a collection that does not exist: existence is not leaked.
access.fieldsIntro: A list of allowed fields, not forbidden ones. An empty list means no fields, not all of them: responses carry an empty data. The delete, publish and schema actions never consult it.
access.fieldsEmpty: No read, create or update grants — the allow-list appears with them.
access.fieldsNoneWarning: No fields — data comes back empty.
access.noSchemaFields: The collection schema has no fields — nothing to allow.
access.unavailable: Access management is not reachable through the gateway: collections-service implements it, the gateway does not route /v1/workspaces/:id/roles and /v1/collections/:id/grants.
access.errorNameTaken: That role name is already taken in this workspace.
access.errorBuiltin: A built-in role cannot be renamed or deleted.
access.errorRoleInUse: The role is held by a member or a token — release it first.
access.errorKindInvalid: Role kind must be admin or consumer.
access.errorRoleNotInProject: The role does not belong to this workspace.
access.errorOwnerImmutable: The workspace owner always stays in it with the owner role — they cannot be removed or given another role.
access.errorOwnerRoleNotGrantable: Only the workspace owner holds the owner role — it cannot be given to a member.
access.errorManyStorages: This workspace has more than one collections storage — members cannot be assigned here. Contact support.
access.errorRoleIdInvalid: The role was not recognised. Reload the page and pick a role from the list.
access.errorGrantExists: A grant for this role and action already exists.

footnote.squash: One person's edits within a minute are merged into one row: the row's time is the start of that minute, its content is the state at the end of it. Someone else's edit and a restore never share that minute.
footnote.appendOnly: Rows are only ever appended: neither an edit nor a restore erases anything from the history. Rows shown: {shown} of {total}.

compare.title: Revision {left} vs. revision {right}
compare.description: Left: what was in revision {left}. Right: what is in revision {right}. Blocks are compared, not lines of text.

compare.same: The content of these revisions is the same.

restoreConfirm.title: Restore the page to revision {target}?
restoreConfirm.description: The content of revision {target} becomes the page's current content.
restoreConfirm.keeps: The history stays intact. A new row — “restored from {target}” — is added, and the current content stays as revision {current}, so you can go back to it the same way.
restoreConfirm.published: Address {path} is published — visitors will see the restored content as soon as it is saved.
restoreConfirm.unpublished: Address {path} isn't published, so visitors won't be affected.
restoreConfirm.unsavedLost: Unsaved edits open in the editor in another tab will be lost: they aren't in the history, so there is nothing to restore them from.

conflict.title: Couldn't restore
conflict.description: The page was changed while you were viewing the history.
conflict.label: out of sync
conflict.versions: The history was opened at version {seenVersion}; the page is now at version {actualVersion}. Revision {target} is still there, but restoring it now has to happen on top of the latest content.
conflict.versionsUnknown: The history was opened at version {seenVersion}; the page has been saved since. Revision {target} is still there, but restoring it now has to happen on top of the latest content.
conflict.why: Restoring would write the old snapshot over someone else's edit without showing it to you. That's why refresh is the only button: after it you can see what changed, and you can restore revision {target} again.

intro.library: Workspace files: images and documents you insert into pages and records.

intro.quota: The workspace is running out of space.

files.nothingFound: No files match this search or filter.
files.truncated: Showing the first {shown} of {total} files. Narrow the search to find the rest.

quota.label: Workspace storage
quota.warningTitle: Almost out of space — the next upload won’t go through
quota.warningBody: {free} free, and a single file can be up to {max}. Free up space by deleting what you don’t need — start with the largest files. Re-uploading a file that is already here goes through regardless: identical files never take up space twice.
quota.lowBody: {free} free. A single file can be up to {max} — once less than that is left, uploads start failing. Free up space by deleting what you don’t need, starting with the largest files.

upload.title: Uploading — {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
upload.description: Files go straight to storage, each on its own: one that fails doesn’t cancel the rest.
upload.explainChecking: The bytes are already in storage. Now verifying the contents are what they claim to be.
upload.explainDeduplicated: This file is already in the workspace. It wasn't uploaded again and took up no extra space.
upload.explainRejected: The file was not accepted. Allowed: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and PDF, up to 100 MB.
upload.explainStoring: The bytes are sent, waiting for the storage to answer.
upload.explainSlow: Storage is slow, we are waiting — nothing to do on your side.
upload.explainStalled: The file is not lost — the storage did not answer. Press Retry: the file is not uploaded again.
upload.explainExpired: The bytes did not reach the storage and the upload link has expired. Press Start over to upload the file again.

drop.title: Drag files here
drop.body: Images and PDFs up to 100 MB each. You can insert them into pages and collection records — a file lives in the workspace, not inside the page it was added to.

details.publicPending: This is the file's public address. It starts working once the public file ingress ships; until then download and preview stay off for public files.

visibility.publicDescription: A permanent URL. Opens for anyone who has the link — no sign-in needed.
visibility.publicBody: The link never changes and is cached for a long time. Good for site images. Making the file private closes access, but anyone who already downloaded a copy keeps it.
visibility.privateDescription: The default. The link is temporary and works for minutes.
visibility.privateBody: Forwarding a link like this won’t work — it will no longer open for the recipient. Good for contracts, estimates and anything that isn’t here for display.
visibility.noteTitle: Publishing a page does not make a file public
visibility.noteBody: These are two separate decisions. On a published page, a private file is still served through a temporary link: visitors see it while the page is open, but a copied image URL stops working after fifteen minutes. Need a permanent link? Make the file public explicitly.

delete.title: Used in {count, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}
delete.description: Deletion is permanent: there will be nothing to restore the file from.
delete.consequenceBody: Deleting doesn’t change records or pages: they keep a reference to the deleted file, and the image’s description (alt) is shown in its place.

errors.noWorkspaceHint: Files belong to a workspace. Create one in Collections, then come back.

statusHint.trialing: The trial ends with the first charge.

member.hint: Only the workspace owner can upgrade. Ask {owner} if your team needs Pro.

lapsed.title: Pro ended: the payment didn’t go through

workspaceSettings.intro: Everything that belongs to this workspace. Your own name, email and sign-in methods live in account settings.

presets.title: Presets
presets.description: A starting point: colors, fonts, scale, radius, density and shadow at once. Applying one replaces the draft — the site changes only when you publish.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.note: Any business: clean, neutral, lets content speak

tech.name: Tech
tech.note: IT services, SaaS, agencies, online schools

studio.name: Studio
studio.note: Fitness, dance and photo studios, events

clinic.name: Clinic
clinic.note: Clinics, dentists, legal and consulting services

colors.description: Eight roles, each with a light and a dark value. Pages use the light values; a section set to Dark switches to the dark ones.
colors.contrastPassDetail: WCAG AA, 4.5:1 — text on background, surface and muted, and text on primary, in both sets.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Two faces from the Markerloop list — served by Markerloop, not by Google, so visitors are not tracked.
typography.scaleHint: Display {display} · H1 {h1} · H2 {h2} · Body {body} px. Phones get a smaller step of the same scale.

shape.title: Shape and spacing
shape.description: Applied to every section, box, button and image of the site at once.
shape.radiusHint: Corners of buttons, boxes and images. Full makes buttons pills.
shape.densityHint: Space inside sections and between blocks.
shape.shadowHint: Under cards and boxes with a surface background.

scales.name: Name
scales.addHint: Name and size. It shows up in every list right away; the site gets it when you publish the theme.

error.nameTaken: A step with this name already exists.
error.tooMany: A scale holds at most {max} steps.

customColors.description: Your own named colours beyond the eight roles. Section and box fills and text colour can use them. A new colour works in the editor at once; the site gets it when you publish the theme.

customColors.addHint: Every element can use it. Change it here and it changes everywhere.
